title: BUGFIX — batch-produce videos not written to publish-ledger (silent catch)
rationale: batch-produce (educational/entertainment/code-demo) runs succeed daily at 9am but the produced videos never appear in publish-ledger.jsonl, so auto-deliver cannot deliver them to the operator. Root cause: logToPublishLedger() in pipeline-registry.ts has 'catch {}' that silently swallows the write error. Fix: (1) log the error instead of swallowing it, and (2) ensure the video_path is a serializable string (not undefined). Also add fallback: batch-produce.ts writes to the ledger directly after a successful run.

tasks.description: In scripts/scs001/pipeline-registry.ts, fix logToPublishLedger: change 'catch {}' to 'catch (e: any) { console.error('[pipeline-registry] Ledger write FAILED:', e.message ?? e); }'. Also ensure result.videoPath is converted to string before stringifying (to avoid undefined): replace 'video_path: result.videoPath' with 'video_path: String(result.videoPath || '')'. This exposes the silent error so we can see what's failing, and prevents JSON.stringify from omitting undefined values.

In scripts/scs001/batch-produce.ts, after 'results.push(result)' (line ~152), add a direct ledger append as fallback: append JSON entry to workspace/scs001/publish-ledger.jsonl with video_id=result.runId, video_path=result.videoPath, pipeline=result.pipeline, title=result.title, produced_at=result.produced_at, source='batch-produce'. This ensures videos are registered even if pipeline-registry's logToPublishLedger fails.
